task.title: Page finite recurrence occurrences safely
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/863 by projecting deterministic allocation-bounded pages of authored finite recurrence coordinates.
acceptance_criteria: Accept page sizes from one through 1024 and reject zero or larger allocations with typed errors.
Return ordered exact occurrences, truncate the final page, and expose only the first unreturned authored offset as the continuation coordinate.
Preserve checked arithmetic and document that the offset is not a durable cursor, claim, due decision, or execution state.

attempts.diagnostic: The recurrence-store test failed with unresolved OccurrencePageSize types and a missing occurrences_page method.
attempts.patch: Added tests for interior and final pages, invalid starts and sizes, exact u64 boundaries, provenance, and continuation offsets.

attempts.diagnostic: Bulk recurrence projection needed a hard allocation bound and checked continuation arithmetic rather than unbounded collection or ambient cursor state.
attempts.patch: Added OccurrencePageSize, bounded occurrences_page projection reusing occurrence_at, truncation semantics, and ADR-0039.

attempts.summary: Strengthened the zero-based contract during review.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit found that interior-page tests did not pin a page beginning at offset zero and the recurrence anchor.
attempts.patch: Added zero-offset anchor and cursor coverage, resolved the thread, waited through the incremental-review cooldown, and merged only after substantive exact-head review.

outcome.summary: Callers can page finite recurrence projections in stable authored order with a fixed allocation ceiling and inert continuation coordinates.

lessons: A public page size should bound allocation before projection begins.
The continuation coordinate is the first unreturned authored offset, not persisted scheduler state.
Tests must pin offset zero explicitly to prevent one-based regressions.
Review fixes need substantive incremental coverage before merge.
